title: Konark Sun Temple
summary: The Sun Temple at Konark, on the Bay of Bengal coast in Odisha, was built in the 13th century as a colossal stone chariot of the sun god Surya, with carved wheels and a team of horses. It is one of the best-known Brahmanical sanctuaries in India and is now partly in ruins.

uncertainty.note: Both sources say only that it was built in the 13th century; 1201 is the first year of that century. UNESCO and the ASI count the wheels and horses differently (24 wheels and six horses vs twelve pairs and seven horses), which does not affect the date.

when.display: Built in the 13th century CE; partly ruined today

where.modern_name: Sun Temple, Konark, Puri district, Odisha, India

importance.justification: A UNESCO World Heritage monument (1984) and one of India's best-known temples, designed as a monumental chariot of the sun god.
